rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reads the command as declaring the nurturing Lord above all and purifying His beautiful names, including al-Aʿlā, from every unworthy meaning.
rows.anchor: Rabbinin a‘lâ ismini tesbih ile tenzih et yani seni yetiştiren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names unique to God's essence or attributes belong only to Him; names describing divine acts must also be understood free of low, creaturely implications and recalled reverently.
rows.anchor: O’nun zâten ve sıfaten kendisine mahsus olan Allah, er-Rahmân, Hallâk, Rezzâk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 86:15–17, recalling the Lord's supremacy assures the Prophet that God's promise will prevail over the disbelievers' plotting and delay, and calls him to gratitude.
rows.anchor: et-Târık 86/15-17] buyurulması akibinde burada böyle ism-i Rabb’in a‘lâ olduğunun ihtârı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call “name” redundant, mean the named referent, or identify name and referent; Elmalılı says these views all intend sanctification of the referent through its name.
rows.anchor: bazıları da isim müsemmânın aynıdır demiş iseler de hepsinin murâdı

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains glorifying God's name as freeing it from invalid meanings such as anthropomorphism and protecting its mention from casual, irreverent use.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf da تَسْبِيحُ اسْمِهِ تَعَالَى: تَنْزِيهُهُ عَمَّا لاَ يَصِحُّ فِيهِ مِنَ الْمَعَانِي

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Ukba b. Amir reports that the Prophet directed the believers to say the great Lord's tasbih in bowing and this surah's tasbih in prostration.
rows.anchor: Ukbe b. Âmir-i Cühenî’den rivayet etmişlerdir, demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that whenever the Prophet recited this verse, he said “Subhana rabbi al-aʿla.”
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayet etmişlerdir ki Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording might have been “glorify by the name” as in the other verse, but the direct object “name” deliberately signals that the name itself is also to be sanctified.
rows.anchor: Buna nazaran فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظ۪يمِ denildiği gibi burada da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿlā can qualify either the Lord or His name; it is explanatory, since there is no other Lord, while divine names have ranks yet all are beautiful and exalted.
rows.anchor: ٱلْأَعْلَى “Rabb”in de, “ism”in de vasfı olabilir; ihtirâzî değil, kâşifedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exaltedness intended is not spatial height but superiority in perfection of power, effects, strength, and judgments.
rows.anchor: “ulüv”den murad mekânî yükseklik değil, kudret ve âsârda, kuvvet ve ahkâmda ekmeliyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih may be spoken purification, marked by “Subhanallah,” or practical worship: inward belief in unity and acts such as prayer, jihad, and enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: Tesbîh-i kavlî lisânen yapılan tenzih ve takdistir ki سُبْحَانَ الله demek bunun alemi olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih also conventionally means prayer, especially voluntary prayer; reading it here as prayer “by the Lord's name” would require an elided preposition, which Elmalılı calls contrary to the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: Burada da Bahr’da İbn Abbas’tan

rows.speaker: İsâmuddin
rows.claim: Alusi reports Isamuddin's suggestion that “name” can mean God's effects, since creation points to its maker as a name does.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin nakline göre İsâmuddin demiştir ki: “‘İsm’ ile murad eser olmak da ba‘îd değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı finds the effects reading strained because no contextual clue displaces the familiar meaning of “name,” though the following attributes resemble the proposed interpretation.
rows.anchor: “ism”in mâruf olan mânasını mâni‘bir karîne olmadığı hâlde zarûretsiz bir tevil gibi görünür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The effects reading does not mean creation is independently flawless; it forbids faulting it insofar as it is God's work and sign, returning to divine creative attributes and the universal glorification in 17:44.
rows.anchor: maksad mahlûkātın kendilerine nazaran bizzat kendilerini tenzih değil, tasrih olunduğu üzere Allah teâlâ’nın mahlûku olmaları

rows.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh defines God's name here as whatever enables people to know Him: minds recognize Him through attributes such as knowledge, power, and wisdom as disclosed in creation.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Abduh İsam’ın bu fikrini şu suretle ifade ederek yegâne bir mâna gibi göstermiş

rows.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh links this sense of “name” with the divine “face” in 55:27–78 and Adam being taught the names in 2:31; these are the forms by which beings or God are known.
rows.anchor: kavlinde mezkur olan esmâ da bu mânaca isimdendir

rows.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
rows.claim: On Abduh's reading, sanctifying God's name excludes likeness to creation, indwelling in a creature, partners, offspring, and other unworthy defects; the next verses identify Him as Creator and Guide.
rows.anchor: Biz O’na akıllarımızı ancak şöyle tevcih ederiz: O her şeyin hâlıkıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abduh's account broadens a name's conventional linguistic indication to rational and natural signs, a valid metaphor when it does not sanctify the world itself; nevertheless, leaving the apparent meaning is remote.
rows.anchor: bunun hâsılı, “isim”de muteber olan delâlet-i vaz‘iyeyi, delâlet-i akliye ve tabî‘iyeye ta‘mîm etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Sufi account, essence is described by attributes, names are the attributes, and effects are consequences of names, not the names themselves; the sanctified referent is God's essence.
rows.anchor: Sûfiyye mizâcınca da sıfât zâtın, esmâ sıfâtın, âsâr esmânın muktezâsı olan ahkâmı olduğuna göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sanctifying God's essence through His name is apt because speech expresses its purity by pure names, while human minds know the divine essence only through names, attributes, or effects; direct manifestation is an afterlife matter.
rows.anchor: zât-ı baht bizim dünyada ukūl ve ezhânımızın doğrudan doğru teveccüh ve idrâkinden çok yüksek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although “name” can broadly include verbal, rational, and natural indications that turn the mind toward God, its clearest ordinary sense is the linguistic names and attributes conveyed in revelation.
rows.anchor: tam mânasıyla mütebâdir olan hakikat bize müsemmâlarını lisânî suretler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice “your Lord, the Most High” signals why He must be sanctified; the following attributes explain and establish this lordship and exaltedness.
rows.anchor: tesbih ve tenzih emrinin vechine işaret olmak üzere “rabbike’l-a‘lâ” ismi ihtar olunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God creates all things, the Creator is above created beings and free from their possibility, origination, and need for a cause; Creator and creature must not be confused in names and attributes.
rows.anchor: yaratan Hâlık, yaratılan mahluktan yüksek ve üstündür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Aʿlā describes the name, the relative clause would grammatically modify “name,” though creation is properly the act of the named referent; treating the clause independently is preferable.
rows.anchor: Bu surette, ٱلَّذِى sıfat olmayıp هُوَ الَّذي takdîrinde cümle-i istînâfiye olmak evlâ olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also apt to predicate creation of the name because creation is the effect of the attribute of bringing into being and thus the ruling of the Creator-name; Sunni and Sufi formulations express this relation.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i sünnet âlimun bi-ilmihi, kādirun bi-kudretihi, mürîdun bi-irâdetihi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not leave creation as bare production: He formed it in diverse shapes and regulated it in order, an effect of lordship; Elmalılı calls Him Rabb-i adl.
rows.anchor: tesviye etti yarattığını muhtelif suretler içinde düzenine koyup düzgünleştirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord is superior to those He nurtures.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki rab, merbubdan a‘lâ ve üstündür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigns every created thing a measured limit by knowledge and will, specifying kinds, individuals, qualities, acts, and lifespans, as 65:3 states.
rows.anchor: ilm ü iradesiyle bir kader tâyin eyledi: Cinslerinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His determination differentiates otherwise equally possible things into distinct natures and identities, assigning forms and characteristics, whether innate or chosen.
rows.anchor: Cinslerinde, nevilerinde ferdlerinde, sıfatlarında, fiillerinde, ecellerinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He guides each creature toward its created end through capacities, inclinations, inspirations, proofs, and revealed signs, bringing it from beginning toward its worldly and otherworldly outcome.
rows.anchor: mâ-hulika-lehleri olan mikdâra müyesser kılmak üzere yoluna koydu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans receive guidance through reason and religion; Muhammad was specifically destined for prophethood and granted guidance and success.
rows.anchor: insana da akıl ve din hidâyetleriyle kendini ve yolunu göstermekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Study of celestial motion and the states of matter, plants, and animals reveals astonishing divine knowledge, power, governance, and guidance; human inward and outward guidance, especially reason and religion, is higher still.
rows.anchor: ne kadar derin, ne kadar ince, ne kadar büyük ilm ü kudret ile idare ve hidâyet tecelliyâtı görülür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All created capacities and measures are finite; no creature has unlimited total power, while the Determiner, Guide, Knower, and Powerful Lord transcends them.
rows.anchor: Hepsi kemmiyet kanunlarının hükmü altında mekādîr-i mahsûsa ile mahduddur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict guidance to human reason, religion, and prophetic direction; others take it as instinctive life needs, provisions, and uses for living creatures.
rows.anchor: Bazıları burada “hidâyet”i akıl ve din hidâyeti gibi insana mahsus olan hidâyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers the unrestricted reading: human and prophetic guidance is the highest example, but the apparent sense includes every entity being directed naturally or voluntarily toward its goal, as in 20:50.
rows.anchor: doğrusu insanlara mahsus olan ve bilhassa Resûlullah’a ait bulunan hidâyet ve irşad bunun en yüksek misâl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This universal guidance includes planetary orbits, attraction, gas expansion and contraction, falling stones, crystallization, dissolving salt, burning coal, and cellular processes.
rows.anchor: bir kürenin diğerine doğru mihver veya mahrekinde devri, bir cüz’ün diğer bir cüz’e incizâbı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Determination covers every entity's essence and properties: size, duration, qualities, colors, tastes, states, beauty, happiness, guidance, and misguidance, throughout all worlds.
rows.anchor: Semâvât ve Arz, kevâkib ve anâsır, me‘âdin, nebâtât, hayvânât ve insanlardan her birine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends everything down according to a known measure, as 15:21 says; the scope is too vast to detail exhaustively, and the secret of destiny is not fully known to us beforehand.
rows.anchor: bir kader-i ma‘lûm ve bir kader-i mahsus ile tahdid ve tahsis eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although possible nature could receive many forms, the Creator assigns each actual entity a particular temperament and capacity; each capacity is suited to certain acts, and its direction toward its end is specific guidance.
rows.anchor: Hâlık’ın takdir ve tahsîsi ile vücudda her mizac bir kuvve-i hâssaya müsta‘id kılınmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's power rises above every limited creature, so His highest name is free of their defects and believers should trust His command and planning to overcome the disbelievers' schemes.
rows.anchor: O’nun ism-i a‘lâsı bütün bunlardaki mahdûdiyet ve noksan şâibelerinden tenzih olunmalı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pasture is the grasslands and vegetation God brings forth for human and animal use, including plants, trees, and fruits, as 79:31–33 describes.
rows.anchor: o otlaklar, o yaylalar, mezra‘alar, bahçeler, ormanlardaki türlü nebâtât

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turns the fresh pasture into dark flood debris, manure, or coal-like fuel; the fate of disbelievers who scheme against truth and people devoted to bodily pleasure will be worse, as fuel for the great Fire.
rows.anchor: sonra da onu kapkara bir gusâya çevirdi gübre ve kömür hâline getirdi

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Citing al-Majmaʿ, Alusi explains ghutha as a mixed mass of scattered kinds; Arabs also call a people gathered from scattered tribes ahlat or ghutha.
rows.anchor: Arab, perakende kabilelerden toplanmış olan kavme “ahlât” ve “gusâ” tâbir ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghutha is the grass, leaves, rubbish, and foam that floodwater sweeps together and throws onto banks; Elmalılı therefore renders it “sel kusuğu.”
rows.anchor: sel suyunun mer‘alardaki otları, çöpleri birbirlerine katarak sürükleyip getirdiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahwa can mean black, brown, dark green, or sooty dark bay; black and brown qualify ghutha, while dark green can describe the pasture from which it becomes debris.
rows.anchor: karamsı, esmer, koyu yeşil, isli doru

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading describes green plants drying, falling, or being eaten and excreted before floods carry them away as dark combustible manure and sediment.
rows.anchor: Mer‘âlardaki yeşil nebâtâtın kuruyup dökülerek veya hayvânât tarafından yenilip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A more detailed geological reading sees an allusion to combustible turf and the formation of coal deposits; both readings warn bodily-minded people of their fate, as 47:12 compares them to grazing animals.
rows.anchor: Tabakāt-ı Arz ve maden ilimlerinde bahsedildiği üzere karbon (fahm) teşekkülâtına

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: The cited geological account describes turf as combustible material formed from decomposing plant deposits in shallow wet hollows and marshes, often with buried trees, animal remains, and layered sediment.
rows.anchor: Akarsularda ve derin havzalarda ve suyu bazı zamanlar kuruyan mahallerde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth scientists agree that coal deposits formed from accumulated plants, supported by microscopic remains in coal and turf and stems and leaves in adjacent clay, but they disagree on how plants accumulated.
rows.anchor: Arziyyâtçıların bu meselede re’yleri müttefiktir. Ancak terâkümün keyfiyeti hakkında müttefik değildirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported theory says rivers or ancient sea waves buried large volumes of plants to form coal seams.
rows.anchor: Bazıları demişlerdir ki: Rüsûbât-ı fahmiye enhâr sularının yahut mukaddemâ bazı yerlerde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another theory places most deposits in basin-like hollows on exposed land, where water carried nearby plant remains.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da demiştir ki: Bu rüsûbâtın ekserisi mekşuf arzın havzımsı hufrelerinde oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the transport theory because thick seams would require implausibly deep masses of floating vegetation; the required plant layers exceed what rivers or seas could carry.
rows.anchor: Evvelki kavil merduddur. Çünkü bu surette bazı bilâdda bulunan tabakalar gibi cidden kalın kömür tabakaları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers local accumulation in land hollows plausible because it requires only the long time needed for organic matter to accumulate.
rows.anchor: İkinci kavilde ise su‘ûbet yoktur. Bu ancak taş kömürün tekevvün ettiği uzvî maddelerin terâküm etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account estimates that modern forest growth could build a thin coal layer over centuries, while ancient carbon-rich air and carbonic gas rising from Earth may have accelerated plant growth and carbon fixation.
rows.anchor: eski zamanda cev birtakım buharlarla meşhun idi, ondan cidden kuvvetli bir nebat olmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coal deposits are not the only formations requiring vast time; thick fossil limestone made from shells also takes many ages.
rows.anchor: rüsûbât-ı haceriyenin tekevvünü kurûn-i adîde iktizâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The turf analogy is supported by microscopic remains of aquatic plant spores in coal and turf, rooted standing trees and fossil leaves, and separate deposits across basins, all indicating marshland hollows.
rows.anchor: Rüsûbât-ı fahmiyeyi turba teşbih edenlerin re’yi şununla da müeyyeddir

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: The geological account proposes that Earth was initially flat, mountainless, and water-covered; early simple algae and sulfur-family plants were unusually large and abundant, and later burial and transformation produced coal.
rows.anchor: Arz’ı örten acîb nebatların kesretiyle muttasıftır

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: Coal-producing plants predated animals; mountain formation buried them deeply, where later changes and slow decomposition infused the material with pitch and tar.
rows.anchor: Devr-i fahmî nebâtı zamanımızdaki nebâta bi’l-külliye muhaliftir

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: The account attributes the enormous ancient flora to a hot, humid, foggy climate and infers similar temperatures across latitudes from fossil plants found from equatorial to polar regions.
rows.anchor: Müstemir yağmurlar, şiddetli harâret, müstemir sisle mestur hafif ziyâ

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: The later coal period features persistent rain, extreme heat, fog, and dim light, producing flora unlike anything possible today.
rows.anchor: bunlardan husûsî bir nebat tevellüd ediyormuş ki zamanımızda ona benzerinin husûlü kābil olmuyor

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: To picture the later coal flora, the account compares it to perpetually rainy, hot, mist-covered islands with giant fern forests, thick undergrowth, and many more fern and seed-plant species than survive today.
rows.anchor: senenin üç yüz günü yağmur düşen

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: Fossil European coal beds contain about 250 fern species and over 120 naked-seeded plants, compared with about 50 and 25 living species respectively.
rows.anchor: Avrupa’da fahmî araziden kazılan serhasiye envâ‘ı iki yüz elli nevidir

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: Geologists agree that coal results from slight decomposition of plants remaining in the earth; seams preserve their stems, leaves, and sometimes large tree trunks.
rows.anchor: Taş kömürü uzun müddet arzda kalan nebâtâttaki cüz’î tehallülün neticesinden ibaret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of two explanations, Elmalılı calls transport of plants from afar unlikely and local growth and decay in marshes more plausible, given the time needed for organic matter to accumulate.
rows.anchor: evvelki ihtimal ba‘îd, ikinci ihtimal akla karibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parallel seams and preserved fine impressions indicate that coal layers formed in complete quiet, from plants dying and decomposing where they grew in marshy places.
rows.anchor: bu tabakalar tam bir sükûnetle tekevvün etmiştir

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: The account imagines a thin elastic crust above a fluid mass; lunar and solar tides and gradual subsidence repeatedly submerged forests, then allowed new forests to grow, accumulating plant layers over ages.
rows.anchor: Şimdiki denizlerimiz gibi Ay ve Güneş’in câzibelerine tebe‘an içindeki seyyal kütle

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: Submerged, sponge-like plant matter slightly rotted and fermented; mineral gases were thought to enter it, while pitchy oils formed during slow decomposition.
rows.anchor: O suların bürüdüğü nebatların kütleleri hafif, isfencî idi, el’an bataklıklarda tekevvün eden turba benziyordu

rows.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
rows.claim: Burial pressure and heat from Earth's interior densified coal, making lower seams drier and harder; experiments pressing heated wood in wet clay with gases trapped produced glossy or dull coal-like material.
rows.anchor: Defe‘ât ile mükerrer tecribelerden fahm-ı hacerînin keyfiyyet-i tekevvünü tevazzuh etmiş
